bugs.summary: ServeHTTP swaps the shared container's Logger for a per-request ContextLogger and restores it in a defer; with concurrent requests (net/http serves each on its own goroutine, all handlers share one *container.Container) this is a data race: request A's handler code (c.Logger, and the goroutine's h.container.Logger at :87/:91) logs with request B's trace ID, and interleaved restores can leave another request's ContextLogger installed permanently, stamping a stale trace ID on all later logs.
bugs.evidence: handler.go:71-75 `origLogger := h.container.Logger; ... h.container.Logger = ctxLogger; defer func() { h.container.Logger = origLogger }()`. The container is one shared pointer: handler.go:41 `container *container.Container`, rest.go:45-47 every route gets `handler{..., container: a.container}`, gofr.go:106-108 same for catch-all; context.go:25/144 Context embeds that *container.Container so handler code's c.Logger reads the mutated field; container.go:44 Logger is a plain embedded interface field with no lock. Interleaving A sets ctxA (orig=base), B sets ctxB (orig=ctxA), A restores base, B restores ctxA leaves ctxA installed forever. AACR human Repo-Level comment on handler.go:66-73 plus AI comment on :86-91. The same PR's final head 0cdac32a89 fixed it by keeping a per-request logger on the Context (`reqLogger := logging.NewContextLogger(c, h.container.Logger); c.ContextLogger = *reqLogger`) and no longer writing h.container.Logger.

rejected.was: model cluster: shared container logger swap races / leaks trace IDs (handler.go:66-79, ~25 findings)
model cluster: handler goroutine reads h.container.Logger after the deferred restore on timeout (handler.go:84-96)
model cluster: panic recovery reads the shared logger inside the deferred closure (handler.go:87-88)
model cluster: sentinel trace map is printed by non-gofr base Logger implementations (ctx_logger.go:24-33, logger.go:247-264)
rejected.why: Speculative: container.go:96-102 always installs remotelogger.New, which embeds the gofr logging.Logger (dynamic_level_logger.go:38-42), so the map always reaches logf and is stripped; no non-gofr base logger is reachable at runtime.

rejected.was: model cluster: append in withTraceInfo writes into the caller's backing array (ctx_logger.go:32)
rejected.why: Only possible when a caller spreads a slice with spare capacity, and the write lands beyond that slice's len, so the caller's visible elements never change.

rejected.was: model cluster: user map with a __trace_id__ key is silently stripped (logger.go:72-76, 245-262)
rejected.why: Requires user data using the reserved internal key; contrived, not a demonstrated defect.

rejected.was: model cluster: only the first trace map is stripped, later ones leak into the message (logger.go:247-262)
rejected.why: A second map only appears when ContextLoggers nest, which happens only through the b1 race; no separate defect.
